html:
Photo: Lower half of the constellation Orion with the nebula of the same name at the center
Canon EOS Rebel XTI with stock 18-55 lens at 55mm, F5.6, ISO 400, composite of 13 images of 30 sec and use of 7 Dark Frames. DeepSkyStacker and Photoshop. This is my first astrophoto. ;-)

After 20 days and only one starry night at -20, Saturday evening was welcome to get acquainted with the Meade LX90 GPS 8".

I started with a quick altaz alignment with an obvious tilt of the tripod platform. The automatic initialization sent me to Rigel, which isn't in the field of the 26 mm. I centered it, then moved on to a star that wasn't in my field of view. I asked for another one and Dubhe was clearly visible from where I was, but not in the field of the 26 mm. I centered again. After the initialization success message, I asked for the double cluster. Right on it. The Pleiades. Right on too. All good.

Since I want to do everything at once and get a series of photos to work on processing, goto The great nebula. As it was about -3, the telescope wasn't quite at temperature and the stars were dancing a bit. But the nebula!!!! Wow, way brighter than in my venerable starfinder, which has the same aperture and the same focal length. I swapped the eyepiece for a Meade UWA 18 mm (5000 series) that came with the LX. Wow again!!! Beautiful sight.

I took a series of about twenty photos ranging from 30 sec to 240 sec. Let's say that beyond 60 sec, field rotation is obvious.

A few negative notes.

-The LX isn't very well collimated... out-of-focus stars are off-center. It'll do for now. I'll take care of that this summer.

-The focus knob isn't very "handy".... I have to take off my glasses to get the most out of the eyepiece field, and that makes focusing with the "silver stick" harder. A more precise focuser is on the wish list. Any suggestions?

-The 18 mm UWA 5000 series shows fairly obvious chromatic aberration at the edges. It may be normal and it may also be caused by the poor collimation, I don't really know.

- The stock lens of the Canon Rebel XTI (EOS 400D) isn't very suitable now that my photos are a bit more in focus. I'm thinking of replacing it with a Canon 50 mm F/1.8, which seems to be very good value for money.

To finish, I'm very happy with my purchase (the LX90 GPS). There are things to improve, but since I saved on the purchase price, I have some room to accessorize a bit.

I think I'll eventually go for a 2" diagonal and eyepieces with huge eye relief (for glasses). In particular the Williams Optics diagonals and eyepieces.
